detail.longDescription: I’m implementing auto-save in Angular with a Rust backend (Axum and SQLx) and PostgreSQL. The editor waits 500 ms after the user stops typing before sending an update. My concern is that two overlapping requests could update the database in the wrong order. PostgreSQL table CREATE TABLE documents ( id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, content TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' ); INSERT INTO documents (content) VALUES (''); Angular component HttpClient is configured in the application providers. import { Component, DestroyRef, inject } from '@angular/core'; import { HttpClient } from '@angular/common/http'; import { FormControl, ReactiveFormsModule } from '@angular/forms'; import { takeUntilDestroyed } from '@angular/core/rxjs-interop'; import { debounceTime, distinctUntilChanged } from 'rxjs'; @Component({ selector: 'app-editor', standalone: true, imports: [ReactiveFormsModule], template: `<textarea [formControl]="content"></textarea>`, }) export class EditorComponent { private readonly http = inject(HttpClient); private readonly destroyRef = inject(DestroyRef); readonly content = new FormControl('', { nonNullable: true }); constructor() { this.content.valueChanges .pipe( debounceTime(500), distinctUntilChanged(), takeUntilDestroyed(this.destroyRef), ) .subscribe(content => { this.http.put<void>('/api/documents/1', { content }) .pipe(takeUntilDestroyed(this.destroyRef)) .subscribe({ error: error => console.error('Auto-save failed', error), }); }); } } Each emitted value starts a separate request, so multiple saves can be in flight simultaneously. Rust handler The router has a PgPool configured as its state. use axum::{ extract::{Path, State}, http::StatusCode, Json, }; use serde::Deserialize; use sqlx::PgPool; #[derive(Deserialize)] struct SaveDocument { content: String, } async fn save_document( State(pool): State<PgPool>, Path(id): Path<i64>, Json(payload): Json<SaveDocument>, ) -> Result<StatusCode, StatusCode> { let result = sqlx::query( "UPDATE documents SET content = $1 WHERE id = $2" ) .bind(&payload.content) .bind(id) .execute(&pool) .await .map_err(|_| StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)?; if result.rows_affected() == 0 { return Err(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND); } Ok(StatusCode::NO_CONTENT) } Problem scenario The user types "Hello" and pauses long enough to trigger request A. While A is still in flight, the user types "Hello world" and pauses, triggering request B. Request B reaches the database and commits first. Request A then executes its update, replacing "Hello world" with "Hello" . The desired final value is "Hello world" , regardless of which request reaches the database first. The debounce reduces the number of requests, but it does not guarantee their processing order. The SQL update also has no condition to detect an outdated save. This example involves one user editing one document in a single browser tab. How can I change this implementation so that the backend rejects stale saves while ensuring the latest edit is eventually persisted? If I use a version column with a conditional update, how should Angular handle a conflict when the rejected request contains the newer edit?
